transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-25 15:00 UTC
Duration: 43 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Neal (Redwood SE), Jordan Park (Redwood PS - 10m), Sanjay Patel (Aurora Head of Partnerships), Elena Torres (Aurora Sales Ops), Diego Ramirez (Aurora Strategic Accounts), Priya Singh (Aurora Solutions Architect - joined briefly)

--- Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect): Reviewed pipeline, flagged 2 POCs that need benchmarks and security signoff; next steps agree to run benchmarks and share pipeline spreadsheet.

Transcript:
00:00 - Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we wanted to run through the Aurora co-sell pipeline, quick check on the top deals and any blockers. How's everyone doing?
00:12 - Sanjay: Good, thanks Maya, yeah we have a busy week, I'll jump in on the high priority ones, Elena will take notes on ops.
00:20 - Liam: Quick intro from me, I'm Liam, SE on the Redwood side, happy to dig into perf and security stuff when it comes up.
00:30 - Elena: Thanks, short intro from me, we're looking to accelerate the two POC deals with regulated customers, timeline's kinda tight.
00:45 - Diego: One note, the strategic account in EU, they're heavy on residency and KMS, so that one needs private or VPC option to be credible.
01:05 - Maya: Great, let's go line by line. I sent a snapshot earlier, but Sanjay can you confirm the six deals you're tracking?
01:17 - Sanjay: Yes — Deal A (Large FinServ, target ACV 750k, POC), Deal B (HealthTech, 420k, contract stage), Deal C (Retail chain, 180k, discovery), Deal D (SaaS scaleup, 90k, POC), Deal E (public sector, 300k, legal loop), Deal F (longer term nurture).
01:40 - Maya: Perfect. For Deal A and D you flagged POC blockers — Sanjay can you remind us what they are?
01:50 - Sanjay: For Deal A it's mostly around data residency, VPC peering and our customer's encryption rules — they insist on HSM-backed KMS. For Deal D it's latency and cost questions, they want to compare Redwood hosted vs dedicated.
02:10 - Liam: On the KMS/HSM front, Redwood Private supports customer KMS integration and we can document HSM pipeline; there was a small naming glitch in our last doc where it said K V cash, sorry transcription, but it's KMS/HSM integration is supported via our private offering. We'll send the security whitepaper.
02:38 - Priya (short): Quick note, for the EU account, we also have to confirm audit log retention, which Aurora's compliance team will own in the SSO/SAML mapping.
02:55 - Elena: Do we have a template for SSO attribute mapping? That's been asked in a couple RFPs.
03:05 - Liam: Yes we've got a sample SAML mapping doc, I can share; it often needs customizing but it's a good start.
03:20 - Diego: On the benchmark request for Deal A, they want to see p99 latency at 2048 tokens and cost per 1k tokens. Can you run that?
03:34 - Liam: Yes we can run a Redwood-hosted benchmark — or spin up a dedicated instance for comparatives; baseline will take a week to set up and run, then we can share raw token-level numbers + per-route breakdown.
03:50 - Sanjay: Timeline's tight; ideally we have results by Apr 9 to present at their procurement review.
04:05 - Maya: Ok, Liam is that feasible?
04:10 - Liam: Feasible but tight — we should schedule the run as soon as possible, target Apr 6–8 window. Need Aurora to provide sample prompts and expected seq lengths.
04:28 - Sanjay: I'll get those over. Also on the pricing side, Deal B is in contract negotiations — Aurora has asked for co-terming and a small marketing rebate.
04:40 - Maya: We can consider a joint go-to-market credit for first 90 days; need to loop in finance. I'll bring ACV numbers to the spreadsheet.
05:00 - Elena: For public sector (Deal E), legal loop is slow. They've asked if Redwood can provide SOC2 Type II evidence and a mapping to the public sector controls.
05:15 - Liam: We have a SOC2 pack and an audit log export, but for public sector sometimes they want a bespoke data processing addendum. We can surface the compliance contacts.
05:30 - Sanjay: Could Redwood do a quick checklist that we can hand to their legal? That speeds things.
05:38 - Jordan: (Redwood PS) Yep I can produce a one-pager checklist of what we can surface — I'll follow up after the call.
05:50 - Diego: Another ask — for the retail chain (Deal C), they want integration patterns for embedding search and reranking, is that on the table?
06:05 - Liam: Absolutely, we support embeddings and reranking via API; we can share an integration sample and cost estimates. Might propose batching and prefix caching to lower cost.
06:20 - Maya: Good, please add that to the docs for the buyer.
06:30 - Sanjay: Quick question on joint outreach — we'd like an exec sponsor intro to the VP Sales. Can we get that before next week?
06:40 - Maya: I'll work on exec intro; Sanjay to share suggested timing.
06:50 - Sanjay: We'll target end of next week.
07:05 - Maya: Okay moving on to prioritized deals: Deal A (FinServ) is highest priority, then Deal B, Deal D. For Deal A we need two things: security signoff and benchmark numbers. Any other blockers?
07:20 - Priya: They asked for encryption in transit and at rest details, and for key rotation frequency.
07:30 - Liam: We can provide rotation policy and key lifecycle docs. Some customers want KMS in their cloud — we can support customer-managed KMS in Redwood Private.
07:45 - Elena: Will that require dedicated infra? Their procurement team thinks dedicated instance is better.
07:52 - Liam: Not strictly, but dedicated capacity gives stronger isolation guarantees and predictable latency. We'll include the latency delta in the benchmark.
08:10 - Diego: On costs — customer is worried about per token price; want to see cost modeling.
08:20 - Maya: We should include cost per 1k tokens for both hosted and dedicated options in the spreadsheet; I'll add assumptions.
08:30 - Sanjay: For Deal D (smaller SaaS POC), they want a short-lived dedicated test to compare throughput at peak. Is that something Redwood will do?
08:42 - Liam: We can provision a short-term dedicated pool for benchmarking, though that has some provisioning lead time and minimums. We'll detail options and delta.
08:55 - Sanjay: Okay that's acceptable.
09:05 - Maya: Let's align on owners: Redwood will run the perf benchmark (Liam), Redwood will send SSO/SAML mapping docs (Liam), Redwood will send updated pipeline with ACV assumptions (Maya), Aurora will send prompts and compliance contacts (Sanjay/Elena).
09:25 - Elena: We'll also pull together the procurement timelines for each account and send a priority calendar.
09:35 - Maya: Great. Any competitive intel — are they speaking to other providers?
09:42 - Sanjay: Deal A has an RFP out to Anthropic and an internal consideration of managed options on AWS Sagemaker. They're mainly comparing cost and data residency.
09:55 - Maya: Noted. We'll emphasize private options and auditability.
10:05 - Diego: One small transcription glitch I wanted to call out from the earlier materials — our partner spreadsheet had a column labeled "KV cache" and some people read it as something else; can we clarify in the doc what that means for performance?
10:20 - Liam: Sure, we'll add a short note explaining prefix and KV cache, and how it affects latency for multi-turn chat.
10:30 - Maya: Okay let's open the pipeline doc on screen — (screen share note) Maya: I'll read the top six rows. Deal A — 750k — status POC — target close Q2. Deal B — 420k — contract negs — target close Q2. Deal C — 180k — discovery. Deal D — 90k — POC. Deal E — 300k — legal. Deal F — nurture.
11:05 - Sanjay: For Deal B they asked for a co-sell case study — do we have one similar in healthcare?
11:15 - Maya: We have a health case study that is close, I'll share the deck link after the call.
11:22 - Elena: On measurement — for the POC they want SLA numbers and a runbook if things fail.
11:32 - Liam: We'll produce a runbook and suggested SLOs for p50/p95/p99, and fallback policies; Redwood supports automated fallbacks to smaller model variants if capacity constrained.
11:50 - Diego: Do we have a cost estimator template that Aurora can use to show TCO to their buyers?
12:00 - Maya: Yes, I'll attach a simple TCO model in the spreadsheet.
12:10 - Sanjay: One more ask — can we do a joint webinar with Aurora to show the joint GTM for retail use case? That would help Deal C.
12:20 - Maya: Absolutely, we can plan a short co-hosted session; marketing would need two weeks lead time.
12:30 - Elena: We'll work out dates.
12:40 - Maya: Any other technical items?
12:45 - Priya: Not from my side; just want the benchmark parameters noted: 2048 token sequence, mixed prompt/response, concurrency 16, and p99 measurement.
12:58 - Liam: Noted. We'll create a test harness and share the raw results plus a summary.
13:12 - Sanjay: Ok this is super useful. For next check-in cadence, would two weeks be okay?
13:20 - Maya: Two weeks works. We'll aim for Apr 8 for follow-up.
13:28 - Elena: Sounds good.
13:32 - Maya: Quick recap of next steps: Maya share updated pipeline + TCO model (by Mar 27), Liam to schedule/run benchmarks (Apr 6-8), Jordan to produce SOC2/PS checklist (Mar 29), Sanjay/Elena to share prompts and compliance contacts (Mar 29-30), set exec intro (by Apr 3).
13:55 - Sanjay: I'll own the exec intro.
14:00 - Diego: I'll prepare the account list for joint outreach.
14:10 - Maya: Any risks we didn't cover?
14:15 - Elena: Procurement timelines might slip; we'll flag if anything moves.
14:22 - Maya: Okay thanks everyone, we'll follow up via the shared spreadsheet and schedule the benchmark kickoff.
14:30 - Sanjay: Thanks all.
14:35 - (call ends)

Notes: Transcript has some auto-caption errors (K V cash, Redwoodinference, etc.). Recorded duration ~43m; speakers joined/left briefly.

End of transcript.
